Gene Description

DLG3, also called SAP102, is a membrane-associated scaffold with PDZ, SH3 and guanylate-kinase-like domains. It organizes receptor-associated protein complexes at excitatory postsynaptic sites and participates in the trafficking and retention of NMDA receptors. Its synaptic distribution and effects on receptor composition depend on developmental and splice context. DLG3 also participates in junctional organization in polarized epithelia.

Summary: DLG3 binds the spine regulator FRMPD4/Preso.
Reason: The original human Preso C-terminal motif and terminal-valine mutant establish PDZ-dependent recognition by SAP102. GO:0005519 describes binding to a protein that modulates cytoskeletal reorganization, so this partner class is supported beyond the presence of a PDZ-binding motif. It does not imply that DLG3 binds the FERM domain or reproduces the PSD-95-specific localization effects.

Summary: Retain the positive HuRI association with vitronectin.
Reason: HuRI reports the DLG3–VTN pair in array, prey-pooling and validated-two-hybrid records from the same study. Sequence checksums authenticate 817-aa human DLG3 and 478-aa vitronectin; these records support binary binding capacity rather than three independent physiological replications. Retain the positive association as non-core. Vitronectin is an established adhesion molecule, but the examined evidence does not resolve this pair in its native extracellular context or establish an adhesion-related function for DLG3. A class-specific functional refinement is therefore not adopted here; the interaction itself is not rejected.

Core Functions

Provides a postsynaptic scaffold whose PDZ domains recognize NMDA-receptor C-terminal motifs and whose other interactions link receptor-associated proteins and trafficking machinery, helping position receptors at synaptic sites.

Molecular Function:
structural constituent of postsynaptic density
Directly Involved In:
receptor localization to synapse
Cellular Locations:
postsynaptic density

Notes

(DLG3-notes.md)

DLG3 review notes

2026-10-17 — Evidence-based annotation review

The normal fetch supplied 456 annotations, including 423 literal protein-binding pairs. All source dictionaries, accession/isoform fields, qualifiers and references remain intact. The completed review contains 295 MODIFY, 33 KEEP_AS_NON_CORE, 122 UNDECIDED and 6 ACCEPT decisions, with one integrated postsynaptic scaffold core and no NEW annotations. Three official human products were reconstructed from sequence features and independently matched to official FASTA sequences.

The public evidence guide gives original-source URLs, assay/construct limitations, the fragmentomics crosswalk, exact AP-MS edges and propagation provenance. The project binding policy is applied to supported associations. Generic binding is not removed merely for being generic. Different literal partners can have different actions; no disagreement is based solely on evidence code.

The full SD1 workbook was reconstructed independently. Zero/below-threshold peptide measurements do not establish biological noninteraction. Positive measurements support fragment-specific peptide binding, including modification and sequence-mapping limits. The RPS6KA1 -1 result is qualified as composite-positive; the discordant -3 LYSC value is retained. ARHGAP17 and DLGAP4 remain non-core associations because independent co-complex evidence survives the undetected-tail result. AP-MS-only KCNA4 and ARHGEF26 are likewise retained without unsupported direct-recognition refinements.

The sole core integrates structural contribution to the postsynaptic density and receptor localization to synapse. Actual original human/rodent constructs, rodent splice experiments, and the current short human isoforms are distinguished. Epithelial polarity, kinase/phosphatase associations and developmental outcomes remain contextual. The 1997 proliferation original was not recovered; the publisher response was an abstract-only HTML preview despite the attempted PDF filename. The tear-proteomics target-specific identification also remains unresolved. Neither uncertainty is a removal or a claim of curator error.

Configured provider attempts and their failures are retained in the ordinary bootstrap provenance. No provider-named research content was invented. The protected main publication caches remain unchanged; separately recovered originals are used only with explicit access descriptions. The existing repository and legacy workspace content were untouched by this TMP review.

2026-10-17: binding interpretation and original tear-table resolution

The blanket peptide-binding replacements are superseded. The positive synthetic domain–motif measurements remain supported observations, but the generic reagent-binding term does not add their biological role. Keep these associations as non-core except where independent target-specific context supports the existing GluN2, FRMPD4/Preso or ERBB4 partner-class interpretation. The assay and product limits remain explicit. Imported parent-protein identifiers describe the source of the tested fragments and remain unchanged.

The 120 unresolved fragmentomics pairs retain distinct measurement or identity uncertainty. UNDECIDED is permitted for an unclear assertion, even when the paper is accessible. A zero selected composite value is neither a measured zero affinity nor proof of noninteraction. The new reproducible evidence artifact provides the original workbook rows, every assay value, sequence inputs and parser. Its counts are 1,344 raw DLG3 measurements; 1,221 accession-candidate joins, including 1,200 natural-ten-mer sequence matches and 21 unmatched joins; and 1,203 sequence-supported scientific selections after matching three AXIN1 internal-peptide rows. Selection is not a positive-binding decision.

The earlier tear-fluid access limitation is now resolved at the protein-identification-list level. PMID:22664934, Table II explicitly includes DLG3. Schirmer-strip collection, detergent extraction of pooled samples, gel separation and mass-spectrometric identification support contextual tear-fluid detection, now retained as non-core. The table does not supply a DLG3 peptide sequence or score, and neither a secretion route nor an extracellular biological function is inferred. Absence of a classical signal peptide alone does not invalidate an extracellular detection.

PDZ-mediated NMDA-receptor-tail recognition is described within the single postsynaptic scaffold core, with a direct receptor-recognition source anchor added there. It is not counted as a separate biological unit. Natural short-product descriptions now contain sequence/domain facts; their functional scope remains unresolved, and they are not equated with the historical rat splice constructs.

2026-10-17: HuRI scope and evidence locators

The vitronectin and EIF4H-2 HuRI rows are now retained as positive non-core associations. The array, prey-pooling and validated-two-hybrid records represent stages of the same study, not three independent physiological replications. The original study distinguishes measured binary interactions from their incompletely resolved cellular functions. EIF4H’s cytoplasmic localization is compatible with DLG3 and does not establish a compartment mismatch; neither pair is rejected. These decisions supersede the earlier partner-class refinements for these two HuRI rows. See HuRI, Generation and characterization of HuRI and Discussion.

The Preso/FRMPD4 refinement remains cytoskeletal regulatory protein binding. The original Figure 1 and Results explicitly include SAP102 in motif-controlled interaction experiments, cellular complexes and rat-brain complexes. Preso’s spine and filamentous-actin phenotypes independently establish the recognized partner class. The term does not identify the physical binding surface as a FERM domain or transfer PSD-95-specific localization effects to DLG3.

The tear-proteome identification comes from the separately recovered publisher Table II. That table is absent from the normal publication cache, whose original full-text flag remains unchanged. The extracellular-region reason now makes this access distinction explicit. The contextual detection decision and all measurement-artifact files are unchanged.

(RESULTS.md)

DLG3 PDZ fragmentomics: reproducible source measurements and sequence crosswalk

The published workbook contains 1,344 DLG3 domain–motif measurements, 448 each for DLG3_1, DLG3_2 and DLG3_3. The 396 imported PMID:36115835 annotation rows yield 1,221 accession-candidate joins to those measurements. Of these, 1,200 match the supplied current product sequence through the workbook's natural_10mer field; 21 do not. Three AXIN1 internal-peptide rows additionally match through the actual peptide sequence, giving 1,203 sequence-supported scientific selections. A selection is an identification/mapping decision, not a positive-binding verdict.

Sources and reproducibility

The source is Gogl et al., 2022, PMID:36115835, Supplementary Data 1, sheet PDZ-PBM interactome. The public supplementary archive contains 41467_2022_33018_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx; that workbook's SHA-256 is ada912921164f0a79630c6a714b9ff264a7217ad3e646153ef498eb456206795.

reproduce.py downloads that archive or reads a local workbook, verifies the workbook version, and extracts the original rows without imputing affinities. It reads imported partner accessions from the adjacent review and checks their explicit sequence inputs against identity provenance. The provenance records official UniProt URLs, record and sequence digests, product lengths, taxa and alternative-sequence features. The frozen sequences are data inputs, not predicted sequences or inferred activity. README.md gives runnable commands.

Output Contents
measurements.tsv All 1,344 DLG3 rows, original one-based sheet row numbers, and all 39 source columns. The single unnamed source column has an explicit generated header.
source-row-crosswalk.tsv All 1,221 candidate joins, imported zero-based annotation index and literal accession, original peptide, separate sequence-mapping flags, and selection flag.
run-summary.json Counts and source/input digests computed by the parser.

All 53,760 extracted cells were compared with the independently saved original-workbook projection. All 1,221 candidate mappings and their natural-sequence positions match the prior source crosswalk; the 1,203 selected row identifiers match the individually reviewed source projection. The same parser was also run against DLG4 and its own identity inputs: it extracted 1,344 measurements, 388 source rows and 1,197 candidate joins. That second-input check establishes parser generality, not a DLG4 scientific verdict.

What the measurements establish

The study tests recombinant PDZ domains against synthetic motifs. LYSC uses bacterial lysates; SAPF and DAPF use single- and double-affinity-purified domain preparations. The stated binding-intensity thresholds are 0.1 for LYSC/SAPF and 0.05 for DAPF. The workbook's COMP field selects the preferred assay estimate; it is not an average of discordant assays. Each original assay field is retained separately.

A zero-coded composite indicates that the selected experiment did not supply a quantifiable affinity under its detection conditions. It is not a measured zero affinity, an affinity of 1 M, or proof of biological noninteraction. The authors explicitly discuss possible binding below the detection threshold. Conversely, a non-negative interaction-database flag is not an independent positive affinity measurement.

Positive motif binding supports molecular recognition at the actual fragment, modification and construct scope. It does not by itself establish a native full-length complex, colocalization, receptor activation, partner regulation, or activity of every DLG3 splice product. The review retains supported generic associations as non-core unless independent target-specific context supports a more informative partner-class function. GluN2 receptor recognition, FRMPD4/Preso binding and ERBB4-tail binding have such additional context, described in the evidence guide.

Mapping cases that require explicit interpretation

Imported row / partner Source measurement and scope
28 / GAGE12J SD1 rows 9021, 55785 and 64021 test PEEGKKQSQC; row 9021 has composite pKd 4.03522737. The supplied current A6NER3 product has PEEGEKQSQC. These remain unmatched candidate rows; they are not counted among the 1,203 sequence-supported selections. A positive mismatched peptide does not settle the literal current-product assertion.
47 / AXIN1 The natural_10mer field is an internal-motif placeholder. Rows 8454, 34568 and 47894 specify the actual amidated internal ligand Biotin-GSGSGS-TLSLTDSSVDGIPPYR-CONH2; its amino-acid core matches AXIN1. These are the three additional selected rows. Row 8454 is positive; selection of the other two does not make their zero composites positive.
93 / SARS-CoV-2 E Row 21885 has LYSC/CALIP pKd 4.09810075 but selected DAPF/COMP zero. The discrepancy is retained rather than relabeled as universally undetected or proven native binding.
166–167 / PDLIM4 products The paper's isoform names differ from current UniProt names. Candidate accession joins are broader than exact sequence matches; literal product sequences determine the matched tails. Both mapped native tails are below quantification.
226 / RPS6KA1 Composite-positive measurements are confined to the minus-one-phosphorylated motif. The minus-three-phosphorylated motif also has a discordant LYSC/CALIP estimate at row 21824, while its selected composite is zero. No unmodified-tail affinity is inferred.
383 / WHRN The internal synthetic ligand ends in Y where the corresponding current sequence ends in F. The native C-terminal motif is below quantification. The internal positive is therefore retained among unmatched candidate observations, not exact native-product support.
253 / ARHGAP17 and 408 / DLGAP4 Tail measurements are below quantification, but independently curated AP-MS associations support non-core retention. Those captures do not establish the isolated-tail mechanism.

The 120 unresolved source assertions comprise 117 below-quantification cases and the GAGE12J, SARS-CoV-2 E and WHRN identity/assay discrepancies. The evidence was inspected; the uncertainty is biological or measurement-specific rather than a claim that the paper was inaccessible. Imported supporting entities remain source metadata and are not rewritten to peptide identifiers.

Reproducibility checks

  • [x] The code reads explicit source and identity inputs; no result counts, affinity values, GO actions or gene-specific conclusions are hardcoded.
  • [x] The published workbook version and identity sequence digests are checked before extraction.
  • [x] All output values and mappings were compared with the separately saved original source projections.
  • [x] The script completed on DLG3 and a distinct DLG4 input.
  • [x] Direct outputs, dependency versions, commands and scientific limits are included here.

Evidence Guide

(DLG3-evidence-guide.md)

DLG3 evidence guide

DLG3/SAP102 is a postsynaptic scaffold. The review retains 456 imported annotation identities and distinguishes a demonstrated interaction from a native cellular mechanism. The three current human products are 817, 512 and 366 amino acids; sequence reconstruction confirms the official alternative-sequence features. The short human products are not the rat SAP102 I1/I2 splice constructs used in neuronal experiments.

Protein-binding decisions

The ClinGen Mendelian curation instructions retain supported generic binding when a more informative claim is not established. Different source rows here name different partners: uncertainty about one literal pair does not dispute DLG3 protein binding generally. Actions differ because the measured claims, constructs and results differ, not merely because the evidence codes differ.

Quantitative fragmentomics

Gogl et al., 2022, Methods “Holdup experiments” and “Quantification of binding affinities,” describes recombinant human PDZ domains tested against synthetic peptides. Its Supplementary Data 1 workbook, sheet PDZ-PBM interactome, contains 1,344 measurements involving the three DLG3 domains. The 396 imported partner rows have 1,221 accession-candidate measurement joins: 1,200 match the supplied product sequence using the published natural-ten-mer field, while 21 do not. Three AXIN1 rows additionally match through their actual internal peptide sequence, giving 1,203 sequence-supported scientific selections. Selection does not mean positive binding. Modified motifs and isoform-specific tails remain distinct. The reproducible evidence artifact supplies the workbook extraction, separate assay fields, identity inputs and executable parser. The sheet legend defines COMP as the preferred estimate across assay preparations. LYSC, SAPF and DAPF have different sensitivity thresholds. A zero composite pKd is not a measured zero affinity, and an interaction database’s negative=false flag or literal 1.0x10(molar) encoding does not turn it into a positive measurement.

Positive measurements establish domain–motif recognition at the assayed fragment and modification. They are retained as non-core associations unless independent target-specific context supports an established partner-class function, as for GluN2, FRMPD4/Preso and ERBB4. A blanket peptide-binding replacement describes the reagent rather than that biological role. The measurements do not independently establish full-length physiological interactions, shared cellular compartments, regulation of the partner or functions of all DLG3 products. The 120 unresolved cases include 117 below-quantification pairs and three distinct identity/assay discrepancies. Their uncertainty concerns the literal partner assertion, not paper accessibility. The original Discussion expressly warns that failure to quantify a pair is not biological noninteraction.

Important crosswalk cases are:

  • GAGE12J: SD1 rows 9021, 55785 and 64021 use PEEGKKQSQC. Row 9021 is positive (DLG3_2 composite pKd 4.03522737), whereas the other domains are below threshold and the current A6NER3 sequence gives PEEGEKQSQC. The exact product mapping remains unresolved; no paralog-misattribution claim is made.
  • AXIN1: SD1 row 8454 measures an internally derived, amidated peptide, not a native C-terminal decapeptide. That positive fragment result supports a non-core association at its actual scope; the amidated internal reagent is not a native free C terminus.
  • RPS6KA1: composite-positive binding is confined to the -1-phosphorylated peptide. The -3-phosphorylated peptide also gives a discordant LYSC/CALIP measurement with DLG3_1, pKd 3.62295225 at SD1 row 21824, while DAPF and COMP are zero. Unmodified-tail binding is not established.
  • SARS-CoV-2 E: DLG3 PDZ2 has a LYSC pKd of 4.09810075 at SD1 row 21885, whereas DAPF and the selected composite estimates are zero. The assays are discordant; this is not described as wholly unmeasured.
  • WHRN: the positive internal synthetic peptide ends in Y where the corresponding current sequence ends in F. The native C-terminal tail is below detection. This does not establish the literal current-product interaction.
  • PDLIM4: the two imported isoform accessions are mapped by actual sequence, because the paper’s isoform labels differ from current UniProt names. Both mapped native tails are below detection.
  • ARHGAP17 and DLGAP4: the isolated tails are below detection, but independent AP-MS supports their associations with DLG3. These pairs remain non-core associations. Neither co-complex capture establishes the measured PDZ-tail mechanism or direct recognition of the partner’s functional class.

Other interaction assays

Masuko et al., 1999, actual author-posted Methods/Results, tests human DLG3 constructs, bovine brain calmodulin and a rat NR2B peptide. Human host cells, homologous receptor peptides and exact current human protein products are kept separate. Garcia et al., 2000 identifies SAP102 in a human-brain screen against the ERBB4 tail; later PSD-95 co-immunoprecipitation is not attributed to DLG3. The LRP2 and ABCA1 historical originals could not be recovered in full; the former has explicit positive SAP102 evidence in its abstract and curated domain records, while ABCA1 has independent positive native-tail measurements in the 2022 study.

The Preso study, Figure 1 and Results, explicitly includes SAP102 in motif-controlled recognition, pull-down, cellular co-immunoprecipitation and rat-brain complexes. Its independently established spine/F-actin regulatory role supports the cytoskeletal-regulatory partner class; this does not transfer the PSD-95-specific localization experiments to DLG3. The GPR85 study tests receptor-tail constructs. The phosphomimetic peptide-screen study uses human DLG3 PDZ2 and native/Ser-Thr-to-Glu peptide libraries. The mere presence of a phosphomimetic library does not establish physiological phosphorylation dependence for each hit.

The HuRI original, “Generation and characterization of HuRI,” describes sequence-confirmed retesting. All nine imported pairs have three curated assay records, with exact sequence checksums matching 817-aa human DLG3 and the literal partner products. This includes EIF4H-2 (228 aa), DHRS11-2 (181 aa), OSBP2-2 (915 aa), DLGAP2-3 (975 aa) and the 543-aa Q6IS01 product. All nine HuRI pairs are retained as non-core associations. The three records are assay stages within the same study, not three independent physiological replications. Vitronectin’s extracellular context is not reproduced by the yeast assay; EIF4H’s cytoplasmic location is compatible with DLG3, but the native role of that pair remains unresolved. These limits concern functional interpretation, not rejection of the measured binding. Dataset-wide orthogonal sampling is not validation of each individual pair. RPS8 binding is not automatically binding to an assembled ribonucleoprotein complex; the short DHRS11 product is not assumed to retain full-length enzyme activity.

BioPlex, Methods “Affinity Purification of Protein Complexes” and “Identification of High Confidence Interacting Proteins,” reports gene-level AP-MS associations. The exact DLG3–ARHGAP17 and DLG3–ARHGEF26 pairs share interaction accession EBI-54784725 but remain distinct spoke-expanded edges. DLGAP4 is EBI-54638731 and KCNA4 is EBI-54596288. These capture results do not by themselves establish direct partner-class recognition.

The 2025 multimodal-map original links its primary AP-MS graph in Data Availability. Exact edges 609982 and 609986 connect DLG3 bait node 609978 to EVI5 node 572570 and ARHGAP17 node 599600, respectively. The partner nodes have bait=false; the data are not called embedding predictions or pair-specific SEC/imaging validation. ARHGAP17’s multiple Ensembl identifiers remain a product-mapping limit.

Core, contextual roles and localization

Sans et al., 2003, selected actual author-deposited original Methods and Figures 1–3/6–7 text, supports PDZ-mediated receptor-associated trafficking and rat-brain complexes. The single core includes PDZ-mediated receptor-tail recognition as a mechanism of the integrated postsynaptic scaffold, supported also by the controlled receptor-tail assay in PMID:10026200. Sec8 perturbation supports receptor-associated trafficking but does not equal selective human DLG3 knockout. Wei et al., 2015 uses rat neurons and historical 849-residue splice constructs: I2 knockdown raises GluN2A, while GluN2B effects differ between exogenous hippocampal imaging and endogenous cortical biotinylation. These results support contextual receptor positioning, not a universal direction for every receptor/product.

Van Campenhout et al., 2011 and its supplementary Methods support endogenous mouse epithelial Dlg3 biology. The recovered full-length cloning Methods do not explicitly give the tagged construct’s species/accession. PP1 association and Nedd4-dependent trafficking do not make DLG3 a phosphatase or ubiquitin ligase. The separate 2009 PP1-interactome cache remains abstract-only.

The DGKI original explicitly uses mouse SAP102 and rat DGKI constructs, alongside rat-brain complexes. DGKI is a lipid kinase. The corresponding kinase-binding assertion must not be rewritten as protein-kinase binding on that evidence alone. Inherited protein-kinase binding has distinct PAINT grounding.

The tear-proteomics original, Table II, explicitly lists DLG3 among proteins identified from pooled tear samples. This separately recovered publisher table is absent from the normal publication cache despite its unchanged full_text_available flag. Schirmer collection, detergent extraction, gel separation and mass spectrometry support contextual extracellular detection, retained as non-core. The protein list provides no DLG3 peptide sequence or score; no secretion route, extracellular function or contamination claim is inferred. The 1997 NE-dlg study remains abstract/preview-only; expression differences and APC binding alone do not establish the specific proliferation mechanism.

Propagated evidence and Reactome

The current PTHR23119 tree places human DLG3 at PTN002508431 beneath every imported IBD node. Actual IBD records and mapped experimental descendants were checked, including rat Dlg3 structural-PSD evidence and mouse Dlg3 receptor-level/polarity evidence. The target’s own experimental grounding and a small donor list are not circularity or weakness. IPR016313 explicitly includes vertebrate DLG1/2/3/4 and matches Q92796 residues 2–817. Its family label does not establish a wrong-paralog transfer. Current ARBA00028600 retains kinase binding but its current condition alternatives do not reconstruct the historical IPR branch; that version limit is recorded without discarding independently supported target function. Rat Q62936 has direct PSD/spine localization evidence supporting the ISS rows.

Typed Reactome paths, read through actual event, complex and member records, resolve Q92796 as DLG3 cytosol entity 6794232 in the DBNL–SHANK context and DLG3 plasma-membrane entity 443609 in NMDA, kainate, RAS-GEF and SALM contexts. Membership does not transfer receptor conductance, GEF activity or actin nucleation to DLG3. The postsynaptic-density-membrane refinement specifies the established synaptic pool and does not exclude other locations.

Access and evidence anchors

The machine-fetched publication caches retain their original flags and bytes. Several protected main caches differ from independently fetched originals used for research; neither version was silently replaced. PMID 12738960 is abstract-only in the normal cache despite separately recovered original text. PMID 21920314 and 25555912 have genuine full-text caches. Original recovery for 12713445, 16192269, 19389623 and 9188857 remains incomplete. Exact short quotations appear once at the load-bearing YAML claims; repeated references point back without duplicating quoted text. Quote count is not evidence count. The review proposes no new GO annotations.

    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:36115835
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P11021
  review:
    summary: The literal HSPA5 pair remains unresolved at the measured scope.
    action: UNDECIDED
    reason: All mapped SD1 composite values for HSPA5 are zero, and no above-threshold alternative
      assay or independently established pair was found in the bounded source audit. The actual
      paper explicitly distinguishes below-threshold measurements from biological non-interactions.
      SD1 sheet rows 45153, 58150, 59696 and the exact IntAct crosswalk were checked; negative=false
      and the encoded 1.0x10(molar) value are not treated as positive affinity evidence. Keep
      this literal pair unresolved, without REMOVE or a claim that DLG3 cannot bind proteins
      generally.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:36115835
    additional_reference_ids:
    - file:human/DLG3/DLG3-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md
- term:
    id: GO:0005515
    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:36115835
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P11166
  review:
    summary: DLG3 PDZ-domain binding to a SLC2A1-derived peptide is retained as a non-core association.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The original SD1 PDZ-PBM-interactome sheet reports DLG3_2 binding to the SLC2A1-derived
      synthetic peptide biotin-ttds-FHPLGADSQV, with composite pKd 4.0317897 (sheet row 9059).
      The sequence crosswalk retains the literal P11166 identity. Retain this positive domain–motif
      association as non-core. The synthetic ligand experiment does not establish a native full-length
      interaction or a more specific biological role; a generic peptide-binding replacement
      would restate the assay format.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:36115835
    additional_reference_ids:
    - file:human/DLG3/DLG3-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md

    label: protein binding
  evidence_type: IPI
  original_reference_id: PMID:36115835
  qualifier: enables
  supporting_entities:
  - UniProtKB:P42262
  review:
    summary: DLG3 PDZ-domain binding to a GRIA2-derived peptide is retained as a non-core association.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: The original SD1 PDZ-PBM-interactome sheet reports DLG3_2 binding to the GRIA2-derived
      synthetic peptide biotin-ado-ado-NVYGIESVKI, with composite pKd 4.1853685 (sheet row 7213).
      The sequence crosswalk retains the literal P42262 identity. Retain this positive domain–motif
      association as non-core. The synthetic ligand experiment does not establish a native full-length
      interaction or a more specific biological role; a generic peptide-binding replacement
      would restate the assay format.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:36115835
    additional_reference_ids:
    - file:human/DLG3/DLG3-bioinformatics/RESULTS.md

- term:
    id: GO:0005576
    label: extracellular region
  evidence_type: HDA
  original_reference_id: PMID:22664934
  qualifier: located_in
  review:
    summary: DLG3 was identified in a pooled human tear-proteome survey.
    action: KEEP_AS_NON_CORE
    reason: PMID:22664934 Table II explicitly lists DLG3_HUMAN, Disks large homolog 3, Homo sapiens, and DLG3. This identification was verified in the separately recovered publisher Table II, which is omitted from the normal publication cache despite its full_text_available flag; the public table locator is in the evidence guide and notes. The original used Schirmer-strip collection, detergent extraction of pooled tears, gel separation, MALDI-TOF/TOF and Swiss-Prot matching. Retain this contextual extracellular detection as non-core. The table does not provide a DLG3 peptide sequence or identification score, and this observation does not establish a secretion route or an extracellular physiological function. Absence of a classical secretion signal does not itself contradict detection outside cells.
    supported_by:
    - reference_id: PMID:22664934

  review:
    summary: Postsynaptic density membrane is a more informative supported membrane location.
    action: MODIFY
    reason: The actual Reactome event-to-complex/member path reaches DLG3 Q92796 entity 443609
      at the plasma membrane. The target’s inherited postsynaptic-density-membrane annotation
      and receptor-scaffold evidence specify its synaptic membrane-associated pool. Refine to
      that existing location without claiming exclusive residence, transmembrane insertion,
      or the catalytic activity of the receptor/GEF-containing complex.

core_functions:
- description: Provides a postsynaptic scaffold whose PDZ domains recognize NMDA-receptor C-terminal
    motifs and whose other interactions link receptor-associated proteins and trafficking machinery,
    helping position receptors at synaptic sites.

    id: GO:0098919
    label: structural constituent of postsynaptic density

    supporting_text: 'interactions

      between SAP102 and Sec8 are involved in the delivery of NMDARs to the cell

      surface'
  - reference_id: PMID:25555912
  - reference_id: PMID:10026200
    supporting_text: 'bind to C-terminal ends of

      N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor 2B (NR2B) through its PDZ (PSD-95/Dlg/ZO-1)
